lines.text: Do you know how a vending machine knows your coin is real? It checks it in less than a second.
First, the coin rolls down a narrow track, past sensors that measure how wide and how thick it is.
Then it rolls through a magnetic field. Every metal mix reacts in its own way, almost like a fingerprint.
Older machines used a strong magnet too. Steel fakes stuck to it, and real coins slowed down just enough to land in the right place.
If everything matches, a little gate flips, and the coin drops into the cash box. If not, it falls back to the return slot.
So that clunk you hear is a tiny inspection, finished before you blink.
